headline: Strength returned before running did — the first structured session in the gap was a lift, not a run. Running remains untaken. The pause is now clearly a deliberate off-block rather than absorption.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The single most important shift today is that a strength session finally broke the silence — structured work has re-entered, but through the barbell, not the trail. That answers one of the open questions: the two modalities did not return together, and strength led. Running is still absent since the trail block wrapped, and at this point the running side reads as a genuine off-stretch rather than a delayed easy-day reset. The step floor remains high and steady, essentially unchanged between training and rest days, which tells you background load is real but structurally undifferentiated — it's movement, not stimulus. The recent four-week running total sits enormously above the prior block because that trail week loaded so heavily; the current quiet is the natural counterweight to it. Recovery-wise, sleep has been erratic, and the strain reading has bottomed out simply because no logged cardio load is feeding it. None of this points to a problem — it points to a big block being paid down, with strength now the first thing back on the board.
sections.trends: The year-to-date picture remains dramatically ahead of last year, and the 12-week shape is one of a large, deliberate trail spike followed by a trough — cyclical, not plateauing or declining. This is exactly the shape you'd expect from an athlete who front-loads durability in a concentrated block and then absorbs it. The concern is only about duration: the trough has now run longer than a clean absorption would need, which nudges the interpretation toward an intentional lower-structure phase. For year-round hybrid readiness that's defensible, provided the next building phase actually starts rather than the trough quietly extending.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the aerobic ceiling haven't been retested recently, so the current figure is a stored reference from earlier in the summer rather than a live reading. Nothing in the recent trail work speaks to threshold at all — those were long, deliberately capped efforts sitting almost entirely in the lowest zone. The demonstrated threshold fitness is still banked; it simply hasn't been touched or stressed in weeks, which is fine for now but means any judgement about current sharpness is genuinely uncertain until a faster session appears.
sections.zones: The trail block was almost pure low-zone time — long durations with negligible time above easy, which is precisely right for back-to-back durability work. There has been essentially zero fast or threshold stimulus in this window, so the intensity distribution is heavily skewed toward the aerobic floor. That was appropriate for what that block was doing. Going forward, the distribution needs some upper-zone content reintroduced or the speed side of the hybrid profile goes untouched too long — but that's a next-phase consideration, not a criticism of the block that just finished.
sections.hr_comparison: The strength sessions that carry HR show the expected pattern — moderate averages with the work spread across the lower zones and brief excursions higher during denser circuits, consistent with functional-fitness formatting rather than heavy grind sets. Today's returning session didn't capture HR, so there's no shape to read from it directly. The most recent trail runs held remarkably low averages for the distances covered, which is the clearest evidence the engine handled that volume without strain. Source agreement across the runs looks consistent; nothing anomalous to flag.
sections.calendar: The calendar now shows a distinctive signature: a dense, clustered burst of trail activity followed by a clean break with only a lone strength session landing at the end of the quiet stretch. This isn't the athlete's usual rhythm of steady spacing — it's spike-then-silence. The reappearance of a lift is the meaningful marker: the machinery of structured training is turning over again, even if running hasn't followed yet. Watch whether the frequency now rebuilds steadily or stays sporadic.
sections.personal_bests: Nothing in the current window points toward a PB — the recent work has been entirely durability-oriented with no fast running, so the speed-distance bests remain untouched by this block. The short-distance PBs from last late-summer are the standing marks, and they'll stay theoretical until some sharpening returns to the schedule.

watch_items: Watch whether running re-enters now that strength has broken the gap, or whether the lift stands alone as an isolated re-entry.
Watch whether the first easy run returns at a normal easy HR, confirming the trail block absorbed cleanly.
Watch whether any upper-zone or faster stimulus reappears soon — the speed side of the profile has now gone untouched for an extended stretch.
Watch whether training frequency rebuilds into a steady rhythm or remains sporadic after this spike-then-silence pattern.
